title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a 'formulaire' (1981): a dictionary of 2x2 integer matrices that serves the Teichmüller computations on the neighbouring pages. Page 32 lists automorphisms of the free group F_2=<u,v> (lifts r~, rho~, sigma~, epsilon~). Their images under Nielsen's abelianization map Aut(F_2) -> Out(F_2) = GL(2,Z) are the matrices on this page; for example r~_0 (u<->v) maps to [[0,1],[1,0]], and r~_infty maps to diag(-1,1). The heading identifies a group S_{0,3} (presumably the outer automorphism group of pi_1 of the three-punctured sphere, a free group on two generators) with GL(2,Z)'. Its 'positive' part is identified with SL(2,Z)'. The meaning of the prime is unclear: perhaps a variant in which signs, i.e. the centre -1, are tracked.

The notation is symmetric under the cyclic order of the indices infty -> 0 -> 1.
- rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has order 6 and rho^3 = -1.
- sigma_infty = [[0,-1],[1,0]] has order 4; its conjugates are sigma_i = rho^k sigma_infty rho^-k (sigma_0 and sigma_1).
- epsilon_i = sigma_{i-1} rho = rho sigma_{i+1} are the unipotents 1+N_i.
- Their squares l_i = epsilon_i^2 lie in Gamma(2) and satisfy l_infty l_1 l_0 = -1.
- Hence lambda_i = -l_i satisfy lambda_infty lambda_1 lambda_0 = 1. These are the standard generators of Gamma(2)/{+-1} = pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,infty}), i.e. the loops around the three cusps.
- The reflections tau_i (det -1, conjugates of diag(-1,1)) and tau'_i = tau_i sigma_i (conjugates of [[0,1],[1,0]]) satisfy tau'_0 tau'_1 = tau'_1 tau'_infty = tau'_infty tau'_0 = -rho.
- Grothendieck tabulates the conjugation action of rho, sigma_i, tau_i and tau'_i on rho, sigma_i, epsilon_j and l_j, flagging signs repeatedly ('attention aux signes').

He then writes the standard presentations:
- SL(2,Z) = <sigma, rho | sigma^4 = rho^6 = 1, sigma^2 = rho^3>.
- GL(2,Z) = <r_0, r_1, r_infty | r_i^2 = 1, (r_0 r_infty)^4 = (r_1 r_0)^6 = 1, (r_0 r_infty)^2 = (r_1 r_0)^3>, with r_0 = tau'_infty, r_1 = -tau'_0, r_infty = tau_infty. This is the amalgam D_6 *_{D_2} D_4.
- Modulo -1, this is the (2,3,infty) triangle reflection group, i.e. PGL(2,Z).
- The products of adjacent reflections are the vertex rotations l'_0 = r_infty r_1 = epsilon_0 (cusp), l'_1 = r_0 r_infty = -sigma_infty (order-2 point), l'_infty = r_1 r_0 = rho^-1 (order-3 point), with l'_infty l'_1 l'_0 = 1. These are the orbifold loops of the modular curve.

Purpose: a sign-careful toolkit for the next page. There Grothendieck relates [l_0,l_1], [sigma_infty, l_infty] and (sigma_infty(phi) rho^-1)^3 for an element phi. This is the kind of order-2/order-3 relation analysis that later appears in the definition of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. I verified essentially all the matrix identities by direct computation.
errors: tau_0 and tau_1 as transcribed ([[-1,0],[-2,-1]] and [[-1,-2],[0,-1]]) have determinant +1 and are not involutions. The values forced by tau_0 = rho tau_infty rho^-1, by tau'_0 = tau_0 sigma_0 = [[1,-1],[0,-1]] and by tau_0 tau_infty = -l_1 are tau_0 = [[1,0],[2,-1]] and tau_1 = [[1,-2],[0,-1]]. This is either a misreading or a slip; the transcribed tau_0 actually equals -l_1 = tau_0 tau_infty.

'sigma_i sigma_{i+1} = rho l_i = -l_{i+1} rho' is inconsistent, because rho l_i = l_{i+1} rho. The correct identity is sigma_i sigma_{i+1} = -rho l_i = -l_{i+1} rho = lambda_{i+1} rho; e.g. sigma_infty sigma_0 = [[-2,1],[1,-1]].
The general rule 'tau_i tau_{i+1} = -l_{i+1}' does not match the three listed instances (tau_1 tau_0 = -l_infty, etc., all verified). Those instances correspond to tau_i tau_{i-1} = -l_{i+1}.

'sigma_{i+1} = l_{i-1} epsilon_{i+1}' fails in matrix order: e.g. epsilon_0 l_infty = sigma_0 but l_infty epsilon_0 != sigma_0. It holds as epsilon_{i+1} l_{i-1}, so this is a composition-order convention issue.

sigma_i(l_i) = (l_{i+1} l_{i-1})^-1 and tau_i(l_i) = l_{i+1} l_{i-1} hold only up to the sign -1 for the l's. They hold exactly for lambda_i = -l_i, which is presumably why Grothendieck writes 'attention signes!'.

ideas.what: Out(F_2) = GL(2,Z) via abelianization, applied to pi_1 of the thrice-punctured sphere, with cyclically symmetric generators rho, sigma_i, epsilon_i, tau_i, tau'_i indexed by {0,1,infty}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses SL(2,Z), Gamma(2) and the low-dimensional Teichmüller groups, but not this formulary

ideas.what: Gamma(2)/{+-1} as pi_1(P^1-{0,1,infty}) with generators lambda_i = -l_i, lambda_infty lambda_1 lambda_0 = 1, and the conjugation action of SL(2,Z)/GL(2,Z) on them
ideas.modern_name: Principal congruence subgroup Gamma(2) and the lambda-function (Legendre family) picture

ideas.what: Presentation of GL(2,Z) by three reflections, GL(2,Z) = D_6 *_{D_2} D_4, and of SL(2,Z) = <sigma, rho | sigma^4 = rho^6 = 1, sigma^2 = rho^3>, with vertex rotations l'_i satisfying l'_infty l'_1 l'_0 = 1
ideas.modern_name: Amalgam decomposition of SL(2,Z)/GL(2,Z); extended modular group as the (2,3,infty) triangle reflection group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Serre, Trees (1977) for the amalgam form

deep.surprise_reason: A carefully sign-tracked computational formulary of standard facts (Nielsen's Out(F_2) = GL(2,Z), Gamma(2), the amalgam presentation of GL(2,Z)). Its interest is only as scaffolding for the next page's GT-like relations, which are not on this page.
transcription_corrections: tau_0 should read [[1,0],[2,-1]] (or the image's sign differs from the transcription): det must be -1, and this value is forced by tau'_0 = tau_0 sigma_0 = [[1,-1],[0,-1]].
tau_1 should read [[1,-2],[0,-1]]: it is forced by tau'_1 = tau_1 sigma_1 = [[-1,0],[-1,1]].
The heading 'Gl(2, hat Z)'' is probably 'Gl(2,Z)'' with a caret insertion mark rather than a profinite hat (uncertain).
In 'sigma_i sigma_{i+1} = rho l_i' there is a struck-out sign in the image. The mathematically correct reading is '= -rho l_i = -l_{i+1} rho'.
The line 'rho(sigma_i) = sigma_{i+1} = ...' may read 'rho(sigma_infty)' in the image; in matrix order the identity is sigma_{i+1} = epsilon_{i+1} l_{i-1}.
